candidates.name: catheter-related bloodstream infection
support_spans: She was receiving milrinone at home through a double lumen tunneled catheter.
Tunneled catheter site showed no erythema, warmth, drainage, or tenderness
Initial blood culture from tunneled catheter: positive at 7.2 hours
candidates.why: The patient has a tunneled catheter and developed symptoms consistent with a bloodstream infection, with positive blood cultures from the catheter.

candidates.name: sepsis
support_spans: Four days before presentation, she developed cough and chills.
Later developed: Temperature of 39°C
Leukocyte count: 12.4 ×10³/µL (normal 4.0-11.0 ×10³/µL)
candidates.why: The patient developed systemic symptoms consistent with sepsis, including fever, tachycardia, and elevated leukocyte count.

candidates.name: heart failure
support_spans: nonischemic cardiomyopathy (ejection fraction 25% to 34%)
Jugular venous distension
Lower extremity edema
candidates.why: The patient has a history of nonischemic cardiomyopathy and developed symptoms consistent with heart failure, including jugular venous distension and lower extremity edema.

candidates.name: gram-negative sepsis
support_spans: Gram stain from all three sets showed gram-negative bacilli
candidates.why: The patient developed sepsis with gram-negative bacilli, suggesting a gram-negative sepsis.
